newsitem.title: COMOROS: Ruling party has 36 of 43 seats in Comoran assembly.
newsitem.headline: Ruling party has 36 of 43 seats in Comoran assembly.

text.p: The ruling party in the Comoro islands, the National Rally for Development, won four of the six seats at stake in the second round of parliamentary elections and now holds 36 of the 43 seats in the federal assembly, government radio said on Monday.
The leader of the Islamist National Front for Justice (NFJ), Ahmed Abdallah Sambi, won his seat in the town of Mutsamudu in the voting on Sunday, bringing the NFJ's total to three seats.
Sambi, known locally as the Ayatollah because of his Islamic education in the Iranian city of Qom, is expected to be one of the most outspoken members of the new parliament.
The other four seats have gone to independent candidates, three of them reliable supporters of the government.

The main opposition alliance, the Forum for National Recovery, boycotted the vote in the former French colony, saying it wanted elections for a constituent assembly, a revision of electoral registers and a new independent electoral commission.
The second round was between the top two candidates in constituencies where no candidate won at least 50 percent of the vote in the first round, which took place on December 1.
The results become official when announced by Interior Minister Said Mohamed Said Hassane and then by the Constitutional Commission. This is expected later on Monday.
